publisher: Tennessee Department of Economic and Community Development
headline: Taiwan's Acumen picks Sumner County for its first U.S. manufacturing plant
summary: Acumen will invest $20.2 million in a 90,000-square-foot toothbrush and oral care plant in Sumner County, initially creating 50 jobs, with production expected to begin in 2027. TNECD says the project resulted from the Governor's October 2025 recruiting trip to Asia.
why_it_matters: Consider noting that Taiwan recruiting is producing Middle Tennessee wins, and ask which SMTN sites could fit similar Asian consumer-goods manufacturers.

headline: Anthropic launches roadshow for proposed IPO on Nasdaq under ticker ANT
summary: Anthropic launched the roadshow for its proposed IPO of 825,000,000 Class A shares at an expected price range of $70.00 to $78.00 per share. It has applied to list on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the symbol "ANT"; the registration statement has not yet become effective.
why_it_matters: Could be useful context for conversations about AI vendors' staying power as you and local employers decide which AI tools to adopt.

publisher: Tennessee Department of Economic and Community Development
headline: Peak+ to create 96 jobs making data center cooling products in Shelby County
summary: Memphis-based HVAC cooling manufacturer Peak+ will create 96 jobs and invest $845,000 in a new location at 3696 Knight Road, expanding products for data centers seeking lower electricity use and better cooling reliability.
why_it_matters: It may be worth tracking data center supply-chain manufacturers as a recruitment target for existing SMTN industrial buildings.

publisher: TN Dept. of Labor & Workforce Development
headline: Marshall Graves named chair of the State Workforce Development Board
summary: Gov. Bill Lee appointed Marshall Graves of Grundy County, previously the board's vice chair and a partner at Stone Door Group, as chair of the Tennessee State Workforce Development Board. He succeeds Tim Berry, who led the board for eight years.
why_it_matters: A new state board chair from a rural Middle Tennessee county could be worth an introduction as workforce priorities for the next few years take shape.

headline: Anthropic releases Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2
summary: Anthropic upgraded its Claude Fable and Claude Mythos models; Fable 5.2 is available on all platforms including AWS, Google Cloud and Microsoft Azure, while Mythos 5.2 is limited to vetted organizations through verification programs. Standard pricing is $8 per million input tokens and $40 per million output tokens.
why_it_matters: A more capable model available inside common tools may be worth testing for research and report-drafting tasks in Greg's workflow.

headline: TNECD makes the case for German medtech companies locating in Tennessee
summary: TNECD's Germany business development director writes that German medtech firms are looking to the U.S., citing Tennessee's third-place national rank in medtech production and exports and more than 115 German companies employing nearly 20,000 people in the state.
why_it_matters: May be worth flagging SMTN sites and workforce assets to TNECD's Germany team as a possible fit for small and midsized German medtech manufacturers.

headline: U.S. added 165,000 jobs in October; unemployment fell to 4.1%
summary: The October jobs report showed the U.S. economy added 165,000 jobs, and the unemployment rate dipped slightly to 4.1%.
why_it_matters: A stronger-than-expected national hiring report could shape the Fed's December rate decision and borrowing costs for expansion projects.

headline: BWXT to invest $714.5 million and create 181 jobs in Jonesborough, Washington County
summary: BWXT will invest $714.5 million in Jonesborough to produce High Purity Depleted Uranium (HPDU) metal, creating 181 new jobs. The project is supported by a TNECD economic development grant through the Nuclear Energy Fund.
why_it_matters: Consider it a signal that Tennessee's Nuclear Energy Fund is actively landing projects; worth watching for supplier or nuclear-adjacent prospects that could fit SMTN sites.

headline: ABB to invest $50 million and create 227 jobs in Selmer, McNairy County
summary: ABB's Industrial Connections & Solutions division will invest $50 million in a new 120,000-square-foot facility in Selmer that will make and distribute busway and bus plug systems and other electrical products, creating 227 new jobs.
why_it_matters: A rural West Tennessee electrical-equipment win may be a useful comparable when pitching SMTN sites to grid and data-center supply-chain manufacturers.

headline: Three SMTN towns win Downtown Improvement Grants
summary: TNECD awarded 14 grants totaling $3,900,568. In Southern Middle Tennessee: Centerville $300,000, Collinwood $125,000 and Mount Pleasant $325,000, each with a 25% local match.
why_it_matters: Three of your communities have match and timeline obligations now; good moment to check in on project scopes and contractor readiness.

headline: Fed held rates on Oct. 28; two members favored a hike
summary: The FOMC held the target range at 3.75%-4.00% by a 10-2 vote; two members preferred a quarter-point increase.
why_it_matters: With borrowing costs elevated, grant and incentive dollars (Site Development, EDA, USDA) carry more weight in rural project financing.

headline: Marshall County selected for a TNECD housing market analysis
summary: TNECD and Points Consulting will analyze housing needs in 14 counties; Marshall is the only Southern Middle Tennessee county selected.
why_it_matters: Housing is a recurring constraint in prospect conversations; the analysis gives Marshall County data to use with developers and recruits.

publisher: TN Dept. of Labor & Workforce Development
headline: Perry County had Tennessee's highest county unemployment rate in September, 5.1%
summary: Unemployment rates fell in all 95 Tennessee counties in September, and 93 counties were below 5%. Perry County had the highest rate at 5.1%, down four-tenths of a percentage point from August.
why_it_matters: Perry County's position at the top of the state list may be useful context for prioritizing workforce and recruitment support there.

headline: September state revenues beat budget by $335.9 million
summary: Tennessee collected $2.5B in September, $335.9M over estimate and 15.09% above September 2025, led by franchise and excise taxes. Year to date, collections are $390.5M above estimate.
why_it_matters: Strong collections support state appetite for economic development grants in the next budget cycle.

publisher: TN Dept. of Labor & Workforce Development
headline: Tennessee unemployment held at 3.4% in September
summary: Seasonally adjusted, unchanged for a third month and 0.1 point below a year ago (U.S. 4.2%). Tennessee added 28,400 nonfarm jobs over the year and 2,500 over the month.
why_it_matters: A tight statewide labor market means workforce availability, not sites, is often the deciding factor for SMTN prospects.

headline: TVA gets $250 million from the U.S. Department of Energy for grid upgrades
summary: Federal and TVA officials said the money will lower power costs and ease congestion, without saying by how much. TVA said it is tied to five transmission lines, none directly connected to a data center.
why_it_matters: Transmission capacity drives how fast large-load prospects can be served in the Valley; worth asking TVA Economic Development which corridors benefit.

headline: TVA's data center rate took effect October 1
summary: TVA's board approved a rate for large data center loads averaging about a 10% increase, phased over three years. TVA projects data center load of 9 to 33 GW by 2040.
why_it_matters: Useful context when counties field data center inquiries: large loads now carry more of their own cost.

headline: Rural housing inflation has reverted toward pre-pandemic patterns
summary: Speaking at the Richmond Fed's rural conference, Governor Cook said rural housing inflation has moved back toward pre-pandemic patterns, though housing costs remain a significant driver of overall inflation, and tied earlier metro-fringe growth to remote work.
why_it_matters: Metro-fringe counties like Maury and Marshall grew on remote work and Nashville spillover; watch whether that pressure is easing.

publisher: TN Dept. of Labor & Workforce Development
headline: 89 Tennessee counties report unemployment below 5% in August
summary: The state's August county release listed 89 counties under 5%; Perry County, at 5.5%, was among the highest.
why_it_matters: Perry is the region's outlier on unemployment; Tier 4 incentives and an available labor pool are its strongest recruitment points.

publisher: Fox News (Penn State College of Medicine)
headline: Four minutes of daily strength exercise improved mobility and balance in older adults
summary: Penn State researchers reported better mobility, balance and leg strength after 12 weeks of a four-minute daily routine. The study was small (fewer than 100 people), so long-term benefit is unknown.
why_it_matters: Short daily routines are easy to fit around travel days.

headline: Regular strength training may slow brain aging in older adults
summary: A randomized trial of adults aged 62-70 found resistance training lowered estimated brain age by 1.4 to 2.3 years versus controls; the effect did not appear in the heavy-training group.
why_it_matters: Supports moderate, consistent strength work over maximal loads.
